Name: Corrin Lakeland
Question: Is it good or bad to date a 39-year-old while I'm 54?
Answer: I know a woman who was 39 and dated a guy around 54 Everything was good for a bit over ten years. Then he wanted to retire and travel, while she was stuck working. The relationship soured as shed come home tired from work and he hadn't cleaned up or made dinner. Fast forward another five years and he had reduced health and mobility, while she now wanted to do stuff and travel. She ended up missing out on retirement because she had to become a geriatric nurse. To be fair this is a risk with any couple. You never know where or when I'll health will strike. I never asked her, but I can't help but wonder if she regretted the relationship — ten good years for twenty bad ones.

Name: Corrin Lakeland
Question: Do you think electric cars are the future? Do you prefer them over conventional cars?
Answer: Electric cars have already won. I’d highlight that even the alternatives we see such as hydrogen and PHEV cars are regular battery electric cars plus a way of recharging the battery. There is no significant innovation happening with internal combustion, every single manufacturer from Tesla to Tata to Toyota is going all-in on electric motors. The only open question is whether significant onboard battery capacity will win, or a method to recharge the more modest battery. Personally I have no skin in the game and don’t really care what the outcome is. I have a current car (BEV) and because I think that’s the most practical technology for me right now. I have the luxury of being able to recharge at home. If someone makes something better before I buy my next car then I’ll get that instead. I’m not holding my breath: using hydrogen for example requires astronomical amounts of cheap energy (probably nuclear fusion is the only practical way to get enough), some sort of awesome distribution network, and some way to make hydrogen vehicles safer than BEVs in a collision. That’s three massive hurdles.

Name: Corrin Lakeland
Question: Does charging a Tesla raise your electric bill?
Answer: Intellectually it must. However for my household we literally never noticed. Doing some rough numbers, I drive about 200 miles in an average week (30kWh). I charge on a cheap overnight plan ($0.07/kW). So it costs me roughly $2 per week, or $10/month. If I was paying a more normal amount for electricity then my costs would double. My parents don't pay anything, they put in a really cheap solar system (no batteries) and that's enough to charge theirs.

Name: Corrin Lakeland
Question: Who made the universal rule that men and women must have different types of names?
Answer: One of my fun little projects was building an app that takes a list of names and produces demographics: gender, age and ethnicity. What you find is the car majority of names have some ambiguity. Take my wife's name: Andrea, most Americans would immediately pick it for a female name due to the vowel at the end but it comes from the Greek for ‘strong’ or ‘manly’ and is closer to 50/50 in Europe. Equally you will find names go in and out of fashion so you can build a educated guess at a person's age based just on the name. On a large enough sample, you can all but guarantee the age distribution of the database will be highly correlated with the age distribution of the names. Ethnicity is much the same - Steve Kim might be French or Chinese, but Korean is substantially more likely. My own name is quite rare and so more evenly split by gender than most. The top hit on Google is for a non-binary character from Fire Emblem. Before that I grew up in a small town that was pretty monocultural and people really struggled with a name where they couldn't immediately identify the gender.
